title: Watercress pasta with haddock and sprouts

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Every ingredient is a plain whole food or ordinary dairy, with no jars, stock pots or packet mixes.

supermarket.reason: Penne, sprouts, watercress, crème fraîche, Parmesan and skinless haddock fillets are all everyday Tesco items at normal prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a pan, a grater and a stick blender, used much as it would be for soup, and nothing beyond beginner technique.

works.reason: 350g pasta, 400g haddock and 200ml blended watercress sauce make a sensible amount for four, and the timings for the sprouts and fish are sound.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes is enough to shred the sprouts, cut the fish, grate, zest and blend, and fifteen minutes covers boiling the pasta and cooking the haddock.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item is used in the steps, penne is fairly labelled as dried pasta, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: It is a warm November pasta where the watercress makes both the sauce and the topping, so the hero is the point of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are brief, clear and in plain British English, with no restaurant language.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a proper family dinner with fish, greens and pasta in a light creamy sauce.
